payload.claim: This fast path trusts tasks.merged_head_sha as proof the task's current pr_url is already merged, but nothing invalidates that column when a task is resumed. A CHANGES_REQUESTED row is in scheduler.REQUEUE_STATES, so after a crash between record_merged_head and set_task_state, the stuck row can be requeued, re-run, and repackaged: set_task_package (saffron/ledger.py:1547) writes a new pr_url/branch/pushed_sha but never clears merged_head_sha. The next reconcile scan then sees a pending row with a stale merged_head_sha from the old, already-closed PR and marks the task MERGED without ever asking gh about the new, genuinely open pull request — silently dropping it from review forever. No test in this diff drives a resume-after-crash cycle, so this data-compatibility gap (old field, new semantics) is invisible to the suite though reachable through the ordinary requeue path.
